Snoredex — documented Snorlax TCG printings

An auditable catalogue of physical Snorlax Pokémon TCG printings: variants, editions, languages, finishes, foil patterns, stamps, distribution and card size. Every claim carries a source outside the marketplace it came from.

What this is

This view projects the historical Cardmarket candidate universe frozen as cardmarket-search-2026-07-21, plus its verification layer. It is not a complete all-locality catalogue. For each legacy claim it answers a narrower question: does a source outside Cardmarket confirm this printing actually exists?

The goal is to let a collector tell three things apart that catalogues routinely blur: documented printings, unresolved claims, and final application absence decisions — and to keep every one of them auditable back to its evidence and decision authority.

Scope limits — read these before relying on anything here.
  • Legacy candidate universe. Every current row descends from one historical Cardmarket search captured on 2026-07-21. Cardmarket is a provider, not the discovery boundary; source-first expansion is tracked in issue #132.
  • Physical cards only. Online and live code cards are excluded.
  • A marketplace filter is not a print manifest. Cardmarket's language filter over-claims: 84 claims here are contradicted by outside sources. The clearest is KSS 26, advertised in 17 languages for an expansion printed in 7.
  • A raw confirmation is not automatically a card record. 17 repository-confirmed claims rest only on a product/set statement or a sibling printing whose evidence cannot reach this exact card. Their observations stay in the data as needs-evidence, but they do not enter this table or the checklist. The remaining 618 claims are established within the permitted evidence granularity.
  • Contradicted is not the same as proven absent. Only 80 of those claims are settled — by an explicit collection-owner adjudication or a complete official manifest. The other 4 are disputed: a source disagrees and nothing has settled it. They are excluded from the checklist so that nobody hunts a card the evidence points away from, but they are not a claim that the card does not exist, and a photograph of one would overturn the row.
  • Pending means unresolved, never absent. No finish is ever marked unavailable because a catalogue failed to list it.
  • Finish evidence is positive-only except under a complete official manifest — currently 4 units.
  • Every “Spanish” row here is European Spanish. Latin-American Spanish is a physically distinct edition from Journey Together (2025) onward. It came into scope on 2026-08-09 and nothing is recorded yet, so read no row here as covering it.

Artwork & detection review

This client-side review surface reads the generated projection of the authoritative locality graph. It keeps a shared work/artwork group separate from each physical local release, shows the current catalogue-derived detection fields beside the recorded image and evidence, and emits downloadable review proposals. It never writes the catalogue from the browser.

Review boundary. Proposals carry stable graph IDs, before-values, source observation hashes and the projection version. A reviewed import must validate them against the current graph before any generator can change catalogue truth. The projection currently covers 612 card releases in 38 mapped artwork groups plus 50 unmapped source-first releases. Download the projection.

Checklist

Generate a printable ownership checklist from the canonical export. It lists what has been documented, and marks items whose finish is unresolved so they cannot be mistaken for confirmed physical versions. Patterned reverse and mirror treatments are grouped under Reverse Holo, while each distinct physical treatment keeps its own checkbox.

include placeholders

Downloads a standalone HTML file that works offline and prints to A4 or US Letter. Use your browser's Save as PDF from its print dialog.

Methodology

Every card × language × variant claim is checked against a source outside the marketplace that made the claim. A seller's photograph of a physical card is evidence; the marketplace's own language filter is not.

Evidence is graded, and absence is treated carefully

  • Source strength is recorded explicitly: photographed specimen > official database / marketplace listing / fan wiki > owner attestation.
  • Absence is never a finding on its own. A source only counts against a claim once it is shown to cover that category. This rule exists because an absence argument once produced a false contradiction here, which had to be reverted.
  • Only a complete official checklist may establish that an alternative does not exist, and only within its stated scope. Other final absence decisions are explicit collection-owner adjudications after reviewing all cited claims; they are not attributed to a single provider.

Finish family, treatment, marking, distribution and size are separate dimensions

The collector-facing Reverse Holo family includes technical reverse-holo and mirror-holo printings. Exact treatments such as Poké Ball, Master Ball, energy patterns and EX-era set-logo reverse treatments stay visible and independently traceable. Printed identity features such as rarity symbols and contest credits use print-identity. A later prerelease, Staff, retailer or Pokémon Center distribution-promo stamp does not imply a reverse-holo finish.

Two evidence scopes, deliberately

A card row shows what evidence attributes to that Cardmarket product. The finish store records what is known for the set number and language, whichever product carries it. Product attribution is necessarily the weaker view, so a finish can read unmapped (known, but not yet attributable to this listing) or other-product (attributed to a different listing) rather than being silently downgraded to pending. When one Cardmarket product contains multiple physical printings with distinct release dates, the chronological table gives each printing its own dated variant row.

Release dates follow the matching market

Bulbapedia commonly records English and Japanese counterpart releases on the same article. The set's published or translated name selects enrelease or jarelease; the article title alone does not. Reviewed Bulbapedia dates take precedence over the generic API fallback, and linked dates in the table open the exact source page used.

Help correct this

Every row above ends in a Correction? link. It opens a pre-filled form with the row identity and everything this page currently records, so reporting an error is usually a matter of ticking a box and saying what is wrong. You need no account beyond GitHub, and no knowledge of how any of this is built.

One rule decides whether a report can be acted on: positive evidence only.
  • A card in your hands counts. Say so — it is recorded as an owner attestation and graded accordingly.
  • A photo, a listing, or an official checklist entry counts.
  • “It is not listed anywhere” does not. A source failing to mention a printing is a gap in that source, not proof of absence. An absence argument once produced a false correction here that had to be reverted.
  • Nothing to correct on a pending finish unless you have seen the printing. Pending means not yet established — never unavailable.

Corrections are graded against the source ladder in FINISH_SOURCES.md, applied with their source recorded in the evidence registry, or closed with the reason stated in the issue. Specimen reports have already overturned three databases at once here.

Sources

2804 claims are attributed across 901 distinct sources (894 unique URLs and 7 non-URL evidence classes). This section is generated from the registry, so it cannot drift from the evidence stores.

The “Absence?” column is the one that matters. Only a complete official manifest may establish that a printing does not exist. For every other provider, a missing row is a coverage gap and never a finding.
